Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to number 2, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,1). So my guess (down from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go left.
Going left, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,3). So the line goes down.
Going left would leave both cell (4,1) and cell (6,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.

Going right would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.

Going right would strand number 5: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.

The line must go left: down is number 10, which comes later.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
